metadata.change_summary: New self-tuning smooth height-field solver: overlapping compact-support Shepard pads blended with a background plane, exact contact-height interpolation, then bounded coordinate-descent tuning of per-contact positive offsets (delta~0.25), support radius and background weight against the exact skfmm loss. Falls back to the initial level set for degenerate/no-contact fixtures or if tuning fails.
metadata.rationale: Loss analysis: contacts (value 0.5) are also logistic positives, and every label shares its contact's vertical column, so a height graph gives raw phi=dz+delta at labels. A two-sided Lipschitz relaxation over the 70 label values gives a hard lower bound of 6.51409 with optimal contact offsphi ~+0.25. My earlier nearest-contact plateau scored 6.835 because Voronoi cliffs pulled deep labels closer than dz; a smooth overlapping blend avoids those cliffs. Local exact-public-objective score: loss_total 6.519067, contact_rmse 0.2717, label_mismatches 0, positive_voxels 25852, solve time ~4.0 s (budget 120 s) - slightly better than the best measured host source 6.519578. Public selfcheck passes (2D fixture loss 0.093); a synthetic 3D contact fixture also returns finite both-sign output. Tuning is bounded (~150 skfmm evaluations) and always keeps the best candidate, with the supplied initial level set as a guaranteed fallback.

panel.brief:
Case drillholes_3d (40x50x30, origin z=-25, 4 vertical holes, 70 labels: 15 neg / 4 contact / 51 pos, only loss_drillhole weight 1). Full state: /workspace/research.md; prototype: /workspace/candidates/0/solver.py.

HOST-MEASURED BASELINE (parent digest 3d1f8f7e...a818c44f, model cbb120b5...77a7): loss_total 405.0796, contact_rmse 5.564, label_mismatches 54, positive_voxels 1655. The initial ellipsoid misses the x=35.5 and x=38.5, y=21.5 holes and is far from all contacts. contact_rmse alone costs ~62, so contact placement dominates.

KEY ANALYTIC INSIGHT: contacts (value 0.5) get both logistic-as-positive and mean(phi)^2 + mean(phi^2). Driving phi=0 at the 4 contact cells removes the contact term; each immediately adjacent label is then at most 1 cell from the surface, so its logistic term is >= log(1+e^-1)=0.3133. The floor is ~2.5; a surface flat near contacts attains ~3.76 total.

RECOMMENDED ALGORITHM A (plateau-pad Shepard height field; not yet host-measured):
Surface z=h(r) over horizontal coords; h = sum_i w_i(r)(z_i + eps||r-r_i||^2)/sum_i w_i,
w_i = max(0,1-(||r-r_i||/R)^2)^3, R = min(4, 0.45*min pairwise contact distance) (here dmin=6.70 => R=3.0), eps~1e-6.
Why it wins: pads are isolated (R<dmin), so at contact i only w_i is nonzero; h(r_i)=z_i and the surface is flat to first order there. Every label lies on its hole's vertical contact column, so phi at each label equals |dz| exactly: all 70 labels correct, contacts ~0, and the predicted loss is sum log(1+e^-|dz|) = 1.006+1.031+0.693+1.031 = 3.76 (S(1..3)=0.489, S(1..5)=0.514, S(1..9)=0.517, S(1..13)=0.518). The eps-quadratic keeps the contact cell the only exact zero (avoids a thick zero plateau that could confuse skfmm) while leaving adjacent phi=1 on the column. O(N) vectorised, <1 s, dimension-agnostic (drop last axis, works on the 2D selfcheck fixture), well within 2 CPU/4 GiB.
Fallbacks: outside all supports use nearest contact height; no contacts -> soft fit or initial_level_set. Risk: contacts closer than ~2 cells (pads overlap) -> solve the small Shepard correction system for h(r_i)=z_i, or fall back to B.

ALTERNATIVE B (implemented, locally measured): degree-4 polynomial height fit in centered/scaled horizontal coords with hard h=z and grad_h=0 at contacts (12 constraints), soft label anchors in the SVD nullspace. Local public-objective score: loss 11.410, label_mismatches 0, contact_rmse 0.0143, positive_voxels 13026; passes the public selfcheck (2D fixture loss 0.695). It misses the optimum because contact curvature pulls adjacent |phi| down to 0.74-0.91 instead of 1. Improvement would be zero-Hessian flatness constraints or a Hermite RBF basis (Gaussians at several scales + linear polynomial, value+gradient equations), but A is simpler and analytically near-optimal.

REJECTED: degree-2 contact fit (local 7.84, adjacent distances 0.6-0.9); direct skfmm-in-the-loop loss optimisation (budget/admission risk, A is at the analytic optimum).

CAVEATS: 2D variants add weight-5 Procrustes sketch loss; A ignores sketch, so for any 2D sketch blend sketch-boundary pseudo-contacts or B (untested). active_mask is diagnostic only. Preserve both signs and finite values; do not use amplitude tricks. Note the prompt's /artifacts/measured_history/observations.json does not exist; authoritative feedback is copper/history.json. Next branch step: implement A, selfcheck on 2D/3D fixtures, submit; keep B as fallback if pad isolation fails.

ROUND 2 RECONCILIATION (case drillholes_3d). State: /workspace/research.md. Prototypes: /workspace/candidates/0/solver.py (poly fit), solver_plateau.py (plateau pads).

CORRECTION to my round-1 brief: the "3.76 optimum" was wrong — it omitted the logistic cost of the 4 contact labels (value 0.5>0, each adds log(1+e^-phi); at phi=0 that is 4*log2=2.7726). Also hole C has 2 negatives, not 1. Correct phi_contact=0 flat-surface bound is sum over the 66 non-contact labels S(dz)=4.0257 plus 2.7726 = 6.7983 (hole sums A 1.0062, B 1.0309, C 0.9577, D 1.0309). A small positive contact offset can gain only ~0.12-0.15, so the flat-family floor is ~6.65.

HOST HISTORY: initial digest 3d1f8f7e...a818c44f scored 405.0796 (contact_rmse 5.564, 54 mismatches). New best digest e9eb7939...a66ef9 (researcher_4) scored 6.5217329551 — 62x better. No source/metrics for e9eb are mounted locally (copper/history.json only has round 0; the prompt's observations.json does not exist), so its loss decomposition is unknown.

LOCAL RECONSTRUCTION: plateau-pad Shepard height field h=sum_i w_i(z_i+eps||r-r_i||^2)/sum_i w_i, w_i=max(0,1-(d_i/R)^2)^3, R=min(4,0.45*dmin)=3.018, eps=1e-6, nearest-contact height outside support. Local exact-objective score: loss 6.8346, contact_rmse 0.0, mismatch 0, positive_voxels 25352. It places every contact exactly at phi=0 and every label at its integer dz at holes A, but at holes B/C/D deep labels are closer than dz because the nearest interface is the nearest-contact Voronoi cliff (e.g. B 4.69 vs 5, D 4.41 vs 6), costing ~0.30; plus the 2.7726 contact logistic floor.
Poly fit B: local 11.410, mismatch 0, contact_rmse 0.0143, selfcheck 2D 0.695. Dominated (contact curvature gives adjacent |phi| 0.74-0.91).
Thus e9eb (6.5217) is 0.31 better than my plateau and 0.28 below the phi_contact=0 bound: it must use nonzero (positive) contact phi and/or a better local surface avoiding the cliff deficits.

CAUTION: my first phi-space Lipschitz relaxation gave a bogus 2.47 because only one side of each |phi_i-phi_j|<=dist pair was enforced (it jumped -17.9 -> +0.4 across 1 cell). Any rerun must use LinearConstraint(A, -ub, +ub) plus sign bounds.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP (highest expected utility): parameterise plateau pads with per-contact vertical offset delta_i and per-pad tilt (2 slopes) or curvature plus smooth global blend; evaluate the exact objective internally with skfmm on the full grid (same formula as host, cheap) and optimise ~4x5 parameters by bounded coordinate descent (~30-60 evals, <5 s). This directly encodes the winning trade: nonzero delta_i lowers contact logistic at small contact-term/adjacent-label cost; tilts remove the cliff-induced phi deficits. Secondarily, rerun the corrected two-sided Lipschitz relaxation over the 70 label phi values to get the attainable floor and target phi pattern, then fit the surface to that pattern. Keep poly fit B as fallback for degenerate/2D fixtures; for 2D sketch cases add sketch-boundary pseudo-contacts (weight-5 Procrustes still unhandled). Verify locally with the public scorer (expect ~6.5 or slightly better) and check contact_rmse, mismatches, both signs, finiteness before submitting. Do not mutate problem observations or use amplitude tricks; host reinitialises with skfmm. Bounded loops only: 120 s 3D / 60 s 2D, 4 GiB; active_mask is diagnostic only.

ROUND 3 — CONVERGED. State: /workspace/research.md.

SCOREBOARD (host, utility=-loss): round0 3d1f8f7e... 405.07958; round1 e9eb7939... 6.521733; round2 93676030... 6.519578 (new best, +0.00215). Sources/metrics for e9eb/9367 are not mounted; copper/history.json only has round 0 and the prompt's observations.json does not exist.

GLOBAL LOWER BOUND (this is the key result): convex relaxation over the 70 label phi values with objective = logistic (contacts counted as positives) + contact mean^2 + mean(phi^2), subject to the true signed-distance property |phi_i-phi_j| <= ||p_i-p_j|| for ALL pairs, both sides (LinearConstraint(A,-ub,+ub)), plus strict sign bounds. SLSQP converged to **6.5140865** (contact term 0.14518). Optimal pattern: contact phi = +0.269/+0.247/+0.313/+0.247 (all positive), and every label phi = dz + delta_h, i.e. each hole's surface is a flat plane shifted ABOVE its contact by delta_h (delta_A .269, B .247, C .313, D .247; all <1 so signs stay correct). Because every real reinitialised skfmm field is 1-Lipschitz, no solver can beat 6.5141. Best host score is within 0.0055 (0.08%) of this absolute bound: the case is essentially solved.

Note: my round-2 one-sided-constraint run (2.47) was invalid; the corrected two-sided bound above replaces it. Also, the earlier 3.76 claim was wrong — contacts add 4*log2=2.7726 logistic floor.

LOCAL ALTERNATIVES (exact public scorer): unshifted plateau-pad Shepard 6.8346 (contact_rmse 0, mismatch 0; cliffs make deep |phi|<dz); shifted plateau with relaxation deltas 6.554 (coordinate search; cliffs still cost ~0.035); degree-4 polynomial with hard contact constraints 11.410 (adjacent |phi| 0.74-0.91); degree-2 7.84. So a cliff-free smooth surface is needed to realize the optimal pattern, but only 0.0055 is left.

RECOMMENDATION:
1. FREEZE the best measured digest 93676030... as the final source; keep e9eb7939... only as a 0.0022-worse fallback. Do not risk regression for <=0.08% utility.
2. If and only if a branch has spare budget: fit a cliff-free smooth height surface (degree-4/6 polynomial or Hermite RBF, ~10-15 coefficients) to the optimal phi targets (contact +0.25-0.31; labels dz+delta_h), or optimise those coefficients directly against the internal skfmm loss with bounded coordinate search (~50 evals, <5 s). Avoid nearest-contact Voronoi cliffs.
3. Robustness is now more valuable than score: keep the polynomial fit as fallback for the mandatory 2D/3D fixtures; for 2D sketch cases add sketch-boundary pseudo-contact points, since the weight-5 Procrustes sketch term is still unhandled and is the main remaining risk.
4. Before any submit: both signs, finite, contact_rmse and label_mismatches checked with the public scorer. Never mutate problem observations or use amplitude tricks; host reinitialises with skfmm. Bounded loops only: 120 s 3D / 60 s 2D, 4 GiB; active_mask is diagnostic only.
